item.title: MAS consults on targeted updates to corporate governance requirements for banks, insurers, and designated financial holding companies
item.description: The proposed changes build on an established and well-functioning corporate governance framework by strengthening safeguards in specific areas where risks and practices have evolved while streamlining requirements for financial institutions with less impact on customers and the financial system.
item.author: Allen & Gledhill

item.title: Corporate law changes from 20 Oct 2026: Streamlined processes and stronger safeguards
item.description: The key changes span various areas such as updated annual return filing requirements, streamlined corporate formalities, streamlined striking-off and restoration processes as well as registered offices and record inspection updates.
item.author: Rajah & Tann

item.title: Amendments to SGX listing rules for enhanced disclosures on remuneration, dividend policies, and investor relations: What issuers should consider doing now
item.description: Singapore Exchange Regulation has published amendments to the Mainboard Rules and Catalist Rules to introduce enhanced disclosure requirements on remuneration, dividend policies, and investor relations. Issuers will also be required to maintain a website, or a dedicated section within its website, for engagement with investors. The amendments take effect from 1 January 2027.
item.author: Allen & Gledhill

item.title: [SIArb J]: Between consensual and collective justice regimes: The U-turn in Re Sian Participation and the future of Hong Kong position
item.description: The Privy Council’s decision in Sian Participation Corp v Halimeda International Ltd [2024] 3 WLR 937 (“Re Sian Participation”) in 2024 marks a U-turn in common law courts’ approach to exercising their discretion in winding-up petitions where the underlying dispute is subject to arbitration. This article traverses the evolving jurisprudence on this critical issue under Hong Kong law and offers a comparative perspective of other key common law jurisdictions, including Singapore and England.
item.author: Singapore Institute of Arbitrators
